name: How to Prepare Your Attached Garage for Complete Insulation and Air Sealing

step.name: Step 1: Complete and inspect all rough framing and utilities
step.text: Confirm that all framing, electrical wiring, plumbing lines, and mechanical rough-ins are completely finished and inspected where required. Check that wires run through the center of studs and that utility boxes are set to the correct depth. What done looks like is an unobstructed wall cavity ready for air sealing without pending mechanical alterations.

step.name: Step 2: Seal all rim joists, penetrations, and bottom plates
step.text: Apply acoustic sealant or expanding polyurethane foam along the bottom plate where treated lumber meets the concrete slab. Seal all wire penetrations, pipe sleeves, and seams along shared walls dividing the garage from the home. What done looks like is a continuous air-control boundary with no visible gaps or air leaks into adjoining living spaces.

step.name: Step 3: Measure and cut insulation to fit stud cavities friction-tight
step.text: Measure each stud bay width and height, noting that bays near corners or doorways may vary. Cut batts using a straightedge and utility knife, allowing approximately a half-inch of extra width so the material stands friction-fit. What done looks like is clean, uncompressed batts that match the depth of the framing without sagging.

step.name: Step 4: Split batts around wiring and notch around utility boxes
step.text: Carefully split the insulation batt along its thickness so one layer sits behind the electrical wire and the other sits in front. Cut precise notches around electrical outlet and switch boxes rather than squishing the batt behind them. What done looks like is a continuous thermal layer with zero voids or bulges around wiring and electrical components.

step.name: Step 5: Fill corner cavities and header spaces
step.text: Pack custom-cut insulation pieces into small framing cavities around door headers, window trimmers, and multi-stud corner assemblies. Ensure the insulation touches the exterior sheathing on all sides. What done looks like is full insulation contact across the entire wall surface with no empty framing pockets remaining.

step.name: Step 6: Install code-compliant thermal barriers or drywall
step.text: Cover the newly insulated walls with the required interior finish, such as fire-rated drywall on walls shared with living quarters. Fasten drywall securely to the framing to protect the insulation assembly from mechanical damage and fire. What done looks like is a fully enclosed, smooth wall surface ready for taping and finish painting.
